title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 48 (Application for performance on certain day to be at proper time and place)

content.overview: Section 48 provides that when a promise is to be performed on a certain day, and the promisor has not undertaken to perform it without application by the promisee, it is the duty of the promisee to apply for performance at a proper place and within the usual hours of business. Explanation: The question “what is a proper time and place” is, in each particular case, a question of fact.
content.glance: Specified day, application required → promisee must apply at proper place within usual business hours (fact question).
content.study: Where performance is due on a certain day and the promisor has not undertaken to perform without application, the promisee must apply for performance at a proper place and within the usual hours of business. What is proper time and place is a question of fact. Current-law framing: confirm application is required; apply duty of promisee to apply at proper place within usual business hours.

sections.heading: Duty to apply
sections.body: Promisee must apply for performance at a proper place and within the usual hours of business.

sections.heading: Question of fact
sections.body: What is a proper time and place is, in each particular case, a question of fact.

provisions.title: Application for performance on certain day to be at proper time and place

examples.title: Promisee must apply
examples.body: A is to deliver goods to B on a fixed day only if B applies. B must apply at a proper place within usual business hours under s. 48.

hypotheticals.question: Who must take the initiative when application is required?
hypotheticals.analysis: The promisee, under s. 48, must apply at a proper place within usual business hours.

distinctions.title: Scope of s-48
distinctions.body: Applies only within the elements and consequences stated in the statutory text.

misconceptions.trap: The promisor must always perform without the promisee doing anything.
misconceptions.correction: Where the promisor has not undertaken to perform without application, s. 48 places the duty to apply on the promisee.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 48 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Confirm application is required. II. Apply promisee’s duty to apply at proper place within usual hours. III. Treat proper time/place as fact. IV. Conclude.
